description: Every configuration key the mailbox reads, with its starting value. Each key names its one reader: `core` (fgos-mailbox-core, `Limits`), `hook` (fgos-mailbox, `HookLimits`), `harness` (the live hook-cost measurement only) or `setup` (`fgos setup` and doctor only); the loader drops `harness` and `setup` keys before it reads a section. Neither crate has a numeric constant or a default, so a missing key is a load error. A project reads these values from the Config standard layer (core/config-standard/mailbox.yaml) through one Config snapshot; the starting values here are equal to it, which a host test proves, and the crates' own tests start from them. Values are the starting values of docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md section 12, unmeasured on fgOS. Status keys are added by the rung that reads them.

keys.meaning: size cap of a message body; a larger body is refused and the sender is told to send a path or link
chain depth cap, counted on the derived reply chain only
agent-origin send attempts by one sender inside the rolling window; refused attempts count too
send attempts by one sender generation over its whole life, never reset
the rolling window of the session budget, used on every CLI instead of a human-input signal
messages between one ordered pair inside the loop window before the loop guard refuses
length of the loop guard window
pending messages per recipient; the newest is refused when full
pending messages one sender may hold in one recipient's queue
size bound of the per-party refusal and notice counters in a snapshot; the least recently bumped entry is evicted
a message still recorded after this age is refused with a notice
the body of an offered or refused message is dropped this long after its last state change
keys.source: owner decision Q1 of the V2 plan (2026-10-22)
keys.status: owner decision 2026-10-22: equal to mailbox.record.ttlSec, so a settled header is kept one day instead of seven

keys.meaning: time an unfinished claim hides a message; must exceed the adapters' measured latency
offers per message before it is refused with a notice
a silence of at least this long between two heads starts a new exchange
wake sends that take effect within one exchange, both directions together
wake sends that took effect by one sender generation to one recipient, never reset
notices held per address; the oldest is dropped on overflow
at most one notice per (sender, reason) inside this window
length bound of a frame header value, and so of a short name, of a writer key and of a binding's handle the core accepts
keys.status: placeholder borrowed from session identity's MAX_ID_LENGTH, unmeasured

keys.meaning: consecutive Stop blocks that were written and finished for one head generation; the count returns to zero when a Stop passes without blocking or a new turn starts
longest wait for the mailbox lock before a hook skips its drain
whole-hook failure ceiling, not a target: a hook call still running when it passes exits 0 without printing, unless its stdout write has started

largest foreign JSON document the hook reads: its stdin payload and the CLI's own session file; a larger one is refused (stdin: the drain is skipped with the quiet reason OverReadCap, which the entry records in runtime/mailbox/hook-outcome.json, and the mail stays pending; session file: no head)
keys.source: borrowed from the repository's two bounds on a foreign input read, both 1 MiB: packages/terminal-control/rust/src/route.rs MAX_STDIN (stdin) and packages/observe/rust/src/metrics_cli/harness.rs MAX_READ_BYTES (a file)
keys.status: placeholder, borrowed, unmeasured; V5 measures the largest PostToolUse payload of a normal session

keys.meaning: consecutive counted hook failures (a record error other than lock contention, or a caught panic) after which the circuit breaker opens and hook calls skip the drain
how long an open circuit breaker keeps hook calls quiet before the next call drains again

longest wait of fgos mailbox send, inbox and inbox --claim for the mailbox lock, polling with backoff, before they answer lock-busy; a person or agent waits on these verbs, so they outwait a hook call holding the lock (a registering call writes and fsyncs) instead of refusing at the hook's skip budget
keys.source: V7c review M2 (plan owner (agent), 2026-10-23); a registering hook call held the lock up to 135 ms p95 on ext4 under load (code-review-v7c.md M5)
keys.status: placeholder, about 15 times the longest measured registering hold

keys.meaning: whether fgos setup and doctor --fix install the mailbox hook rows into this project's Claude Code and Codex hook files; false removes the rows they installed
keys.source: spec §16 item 23, owner answer 2026-10-28: on by default

keys.meaning: target p95 of a hook call on the path with no mail, measured inside each CLI's real hook environment; the hook itself never reads it
